notes: IMDuel on Ethereum (chain 1): chess played by trades. The engine argument (ENGINE_ADDRESS) is ChessEngineV5's address from the engine launch (launch/engine.json). Constructor arguments in declaration order: manager = $poolManager; engine = ChessEngineV5 (its code is not checked in the constructor, so the hook builds where the engine has none; the address is checked off chain); imd = IMD 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7; turnBlocks 3: how many blocks a move takes bids for (about 36 seconds). No owner, admin, pause, upgrade path or backend signer. The token is src/IMDuelToken.sol on the standard terms (1,000,000,000 fixed, 18 decimals, the whole supply minted to the factory, plain transfers, no owner, mint, burn, tax, pause or blocklist). The factory deploys the hook and the token and opens this pool (IMD pair, fee 12500, spacing 60) in one transaction; the first pool opened on the hook is the main duel and must pair IMD (afterInitialize reverts otherwise), its other currency becomes $IMDUEL; every later duel must pair IMD or $IMDUEL (NoRoute otherwise; there is no native ETH route). Fee: 0.75% of every swap of its pools through beforeSwapReturnDelta / afterSwapReturnDelta, on top of the untouched 1.25% LP fee: 0.65% into the war chests (pots), half from each side of the trade into that token's pot, so every trade feeds both and they stay balanced; 0.1% the protocol slice, taken with no swap: in $IMDUEL wherever the pool holds it (always in the main duel), all owed to 0x...dEaD (anyone's withdraw(0x...dEaD, $IMDUEL) burns it), else in IMD into the main duel's IMD pot. The hook reads no pool price anywhere. There is no opening surcharge and no other charge. Every swap the hook takes a fee from emits URC-2's HookSwap(id, sender, amount0, amount1, swapFee) with the hook's own delta and the rate (7,500 pips); a dust swap whose fee rounds to zero emits none. A swap must trade its whole order: one its price limit stops early reverts (PartialFill). Liquidity callbacks are not used, and no liquidity or price is read for strength: a bid's strength is what its trade received as a share of its own team's pot (0% at 0.1% of the pot, 90% from the whole pot; an empty pot plays at the cap). Anyone can add to a pool's pots with fundChest(key, inCurrency1, amount) (tokens approved to the hook, or exact native value); a pot holds at most 2^128 - 1 and refuses more. previewMove(poolId, hash) returns the move a closed window will play given its last block's hash. Known and accepted: the builder of a window's last block can bid in it and try versions of it, keeping the hash whose move pays. Play: every buy bids for its team's next move; its owner is the address in hookData (20 bytes packed or 32 bytes ABI-encoded; zero, the hook, the PoolManager or 0x...dEaD count as none), else the wallet that signed the transaction, so a trade through any router earns (a trade relayed for a smart-contract wallet without hookData credits the relayer: known, accepted); the biggest owns it and a new top bid must pay more than 10% over the current one; a move takes bids for 3 blocks after the previous one was played (a move whose first bid comes only in its window's last block or later takes bids for 3 blocks from that bid, so its team can answer), and the first swap after its window plays it through a gas-capped external call to the engine, seeded by the hash of the window's last block (BLOCKHASH, or the EIP-2935 history contract beyond 256 blocks; a hash no longer served plays the bid's strength for nobody, the current block its window). An engine failure never reverts a swap: a seeded legal move plays at 0%, and if that fails too the game ends as a draw (reason 6) and a new one starts, so a pool can never freeze; an engine starved by the swap's own gas limit reverts it (NotEnoughGas). Only checkmate pays: a mate takes a quarter of the LOSING team's pot (MATE_SHARE_BPS 2,500) and records it for the owner of the mating move, in the loser's token, capped at twice what that bid paid (PAYOUT_CAP 2) and at what the game's trading put into the pots (MATE_INFLOW_CAP 1, gameInflow: the pot fee only, a trade's fee counted for the game its bid is for; only that game's pot fees into the losing pot count (half of every trade's), in that one token, so no price is read; a game played for dust pays nothing); captures, checks, draws and timeout moves pay nothing and the pots carry over. Rewards are recorded as owed and claimed (withdraw(who, c): anyone may call it, it only pays who; withdrawTo(c, to): the owed party, to an address it names, never address 0; a claim leaves 1 wei owed); no reward is ever sent inside a trade, so no recipient runs code while a trader's PoolManager is unlocked (a trade makes no transfer at all: even the burn waits for anyone's withdraw). The hook also keeps per-address play counts for the main duel only (stats(address), players), for badges and display; they never pay or limit anything, side duels count nothing, and every move a trade's bid plays counts, mates included.
